memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'I will provide for you there, because five years of famine are still to come. Otherwise you and your household and all who belong to you will become destitute.'" — Gen 45:11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
"I will provide for you there." Joseph does not simply invite them to come; he promises to sustain them once they arrive. He knows exactly how long the famine has left to run, and he has the resources to carry them through every year of it.

There is real relief in being cared for by someone who both knows the situation fully and has the power to meet it. Half of our anxiety comes from the fear that whoever is helping us does not really understand the size of the problem.

God is never in that position. He knows precisely how long your famine will last, and He is not rationing His resources anxiously. Jesus pointed to birds and flowers and asked why we worry, when our heavenly Father knows what we need (Matt 6:31-33).

But be careful here. This is not a promise that Christians will always be comfortable or wealthy. Joseph's family still had to leave home, still had to live as foreigners, and their descendants would eventually face bitter slavery in this same land. God's provision is real, but it is not the same as ease.

What God guarantees is that He will supply what His children truly need, according to His riches in Christ (Phil 4:19). He is a Father, and He is not careless.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What are you anxious about providing for right now?
2. Have you confused God's promise to provide with a promise of comfort?
3. Where has God met a need in a way you did not expect?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You know exactly what I need and exactly how long this season will last. Help me stop carrying anxiety that belongs to You, and trust Your care for me. Amen.
